key_insight: An interpretable hybrid model encoded the Alzheimer's A/T/N framework as logic rules while using neural networks to extract biomarker features, improving prediction of incident AD.
clinical_relevance: This approach may support earlier Alzheimer's risk stratification by combining transparency with flexibility, potentially aiding preclinical screening and research staging.
method: Encoded the A/T/N framework as a logic program for interpretable decision-making
Used one or more neural networks to extract biomarker features from input data
Fused symbolic rules with learned features in a hybrid model called Neurosymodal Data Fusion
evidence_signal: In ADNI, the pipeline predicted four-year incident Alzheimer's disease with sensitivity up to 0.84 and produced scores for A/T/N profiles.
watch_item: The abstract notes that empirically derived A and T cutoffs may be uninformative in ADNI, so generalizability and threshold selection need careful validation.
paper_title: Encoding Discordance in the Alzheimer's Disease A/T/N Framework
